title: Older Scholastics allow only mode one (improper adoration); recent School rejects that as rash
source_text: VI. Jam vero nonnulli sunt inter veteres Scholasticos qui putant imagines primo tantum modo adorandas esse; nempe licere quidem coram iis procumbere, & genua flectere, & cereos ac incensum offerre, sed tamen illum qui exercet istos actus adorationis totam mentis intentionem dirigere debere, non ad imaginem ipsam, sed ad solum exemplar imagine repraesentatum, ut ad objectum quod per se & proprie adoratur. Unde colligunt imagines non adorari, nisi improprie atque abusive. Sed in schola recentiori sententia ista, tanquam temeraria & improbabilis omnino rejicitur: & statuitur tanquam certum quid & indubitatum, imagines proprie & vere adorandas esse.
pass_a_gloss: Now indeed there are some among the older Scholastics who think that images are to be adored only in the first mode; namely that it is lawful indeed to prostrate before them, and to bend the knee, and to offer candles and incense, yet that he who exercises those acts of adoration ought to direct the whole intention of the mind, not to the image itself, but to the exemplar alone represented by the image, as to the object which is adored per se and properly. Whence they gather that images are not adored, except improperly and abusively. But in the more recent school that opinion is rejected altogether as rash and improbable: and it is established as something certain and undoubted, that images are to be adored properly and truly.
pass_b_english: Older Schoolmen: bodily honors yes, but intention only on the exemplar—so image-adoration is improper/abusive.
Recent School throws that out as rash and insists images are adored properly and truly.

choices.why: Contrast class before the recent consensus.
